_metadata.title: Cluevoyance Unlimited - 20-word clue-generation pilot set
_metadata.purpose: A deliberately varied 20-word sample used to test whether high-quality pair clues can be generated before scaling to 100 words.
_metadata.source: Selected from data/unlimited/source-wordbank-visible-1000.json (the visible 1000-row subset of the production word bank).
selection_rules_applied: Common and broadly recognizable to a general audience.
Versatile enough to support several different kinds of connection.
Varied in meaning; many double as verbs or adjectives as well as nouns.
Chosen to exercise direct association, shared category, before/after, compounds, cause and effect, contrast, cultural reference, wordplay and lateral stretches.
No spelling variants or near-duplicates of each other (THEATER/THEATRE, STOCK/STOCKS excluded).
Single words only, short enough for the existing card and clue-tab design.
Includes intentionally difficult members (SHADOW, ENGINE, MIRROR) so the pilot is not biased toward easy pairings.
_metadata.id_scheme: w_ + normalized lowercase spelling. Deterministic: the same word always yields the same id.

words.reason: Elemental and extremely generative: compounds (firefly, fireplace), idioms (on fire), and strong cause-and-effect links to heat, smoke and danger.
Celestial anchor with heavy cultural and mythic loading (werewolves, landings, honeymoon), useful for reference and compound clues.
True homonym (money / river edge / to bank a turn). Essential for testing whether wordplay clues can exploit double meanings.
Triple meaning (season / metal coil / water source) plus a verb sense. Tests whether the generator picks the most useful sense per pair.
Homonym across illumination and weight, and works as noun, verb and adjective. Natural contrast partner for SHADOW and MIRROR.
Spans anatomy, emotion and the card suit; idiom-dense, so it tests figurative as well as literal connections.
Metal, household appliance, golf club and verb. Good for shared-category and function-based clues.
Royalty, dental work and the top of the head or a hill. Tests whether less obvious senses get used when the obvious one fails.
Animal plus gymnastics apparatus plus idiom surface (dark horse, horsepower, Trojan horse).
Deliberately harder: abstract, few compounds, limited category overlap. Included to stress-test difficult pairings rather than flatter the results.
Object, musical key, map legend, answer sheet and island (Key West). One of the most flexible words in the bank.
Mineral and preservative with strong idiomatic reach (old salt, salt of the earth, worth your salt) and a clear contrast with sweetness.
Flower, colour, proper name and the past tense of rise. Excellent wordplay candidate.
Gem, card suit, baseball infield and geometric shape. Pairs naturally with HEART for card-suit clues and with IRON for hardness.
Supernatural noun, modern verb (to ghost someone) and compound (ghostwriter). Tests cultural-reference and lateral clues.
Food, colour and term of endearment; the honeymoon compound links it to MOON, giving a known-good compound test case.
Animal, plumbing tool, verb of movement and metaphor for a betrayer. Strong for contrast and lateral connections.
Structure, card game, dental fitting, part of a song and part of the nose. High-polysemy counterweight to the concrete nouns.
Reflection noun and verb. Intentionally narrow in category terms, which forces lateral work on pairs like MIRROR/ENGINE.
Deliberately dry and technical with the least figurative reach of the set. Included as the hardest member so the pilot reveals worst-case clue quality.
